sections.title: Full compiler settings
sections.what: Sets which files the checker reads and skips, turns off output, keeps screen syntax for the bundler, allows the @ shortcut to point at src, and links the API client library.

sections.watch_out: Turning off output means this file only checks code. It does not build the app.

summary: The TypeScript compiler settings for the capital projects app, which check the code for type errors without producing output files.
purpose: Tells the TypeScript checker which files to read, which to skip, which language features to allow, and how the @ import shortcut maps to the source folder.
why: Likely reason: it extends a shared base file so that all apps in the project use the same rules. The reason for each setting is not stated.
how: It extends the shared base config, includes everything under src, and excludes test files and build folders. It turns off output, keeps JSX for the bundler, allows the @ alias to point at src, and links to the API client library.
inputs: The source files under src, and the shared base configuration.
outputs: Type-check results. No compiled files are written because output is turned off.
risks: Test files ending in .test.ts are not type-checked, so type errors in them go unnoticed. The @ alias must match the one in the Vite config.
debug: If imports using @ fail to resolve, compare the paths here with the alias in vite.config.ts. If types from the shared base are missing, check the base file.
